evidence:
Core picture recovery is incomplete. Frozen task/instruction.md:3 requests the actual last good preview including changes made through controls. Frozen task/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:13 explicitly requires the actual latest successful picture, including button-made changes, after failure or Stop; the security note does not exclude ordinary Canvas 2D drawing. In frozen solution/app/src/runtime.ts:150-189, snapshot() clones document.documentElement (line 152), copies stylesheet/form state, then serializes copy.outerHTML (line 189). No canvas bitmap is copied. staticDocument()/PreviewRunner.restore() at lines 17-21 and 357-358 consequently restore an empty canvas.

Independent focused browser execution against cw-stricter-golden-20261001 confirmed this using only ordinary UI actions and a fresh isolated context: a complete HTML file renders a canvas; its Paint red button uses getContext("2d").fillRect() and changes a paragraph to Painted red; execution completes. Before the next run, the canvas center was RGBA [224,36,36,255]. A subsequent JS run changes its candidate DOM then throws canvas-recovery-test. The reference reports Error - previous preview retained, restores the heading and Painted red paragraph, but the canvas center becomes [0,0,0,0]. The before/after screenshots visibly show the red rectangle disappearing. row17-canvas-proof.json (SHA256 5180199ab010452969fb0d96586143853229a506d6f5192cf906dc51f687fa51) preserves exact inputs, status, console and observed pixels. row17-canvas-binding.json records command, proof hashes, and exact matches for running server.js plus every served index/JS/CSS/runner asset against this frozen candidate.

The major requested surfaces do have implementations: app.tsx:15-17 console object/array inspection; :44-115 logs, Run, auto-run cancellation, save/conflict/recovery; :128-154 workspace/library/history/keyboard controls; server.js:52-118 revision checks, immutable snapshots, atomic restore and retry recognition; :142-168 durable SQLite schema; runtime.ts:24-67 guards, :149-269 console/timer/error handling, :299-346 filename-selected HTML/JS builds, and :349-387 isolated preview lifecycle; style.css:1-5 responsive panes/history overflow. Existing hash-verified scripted observations cover these ordinary controls, text/input rollback, history and race cases, but they do not cover canvas pixel preservation. Their success does not refute this additional valid input.

Conforming alternative considered: retaining canvas pixels as a static bitmap during rollback would satisfy the explicit permission for a static restored picture; original event handlers need not survive. This finding does not require a particular frontend framework, label, route, or reactivated handler. No configured judge or portal score is claimed. The browser deployment omits frozen local node_modules, so product behavior and installation evidence remain distinct.
counterexample: Run a complete HTML document containing a 180x100 canvas, a Paint red button and an inline classic script whose button handler fills the canvas red and changes a paragraph to Painted red. Click the button and wait for Complete. Run a different JS source that modifies its own candidate document and throws an Error. The actual reference is a plausible broken implementation that passes text/input-only rollback checks: it restores the paragraph but erases the successful canvas drawing, violating instruction.md:3 and behaviour.md:13. Exact reproducer and observed output are in row17-canvas-proof.cjs/json.
suggested_fix: Preserve visible canvas pixels in each successful snapshot, for example as inert bitmap replacements, and verify that errors, Stop and timeout restore the captured picture without executing old handlers.
